logs.title: House Rules
logs.text:
House rules, galley of the Tin Mother.
Rule 1: the soup is whatever is in the pot.
Rule 2: do not ask about Rule 1.
Rule 3: seconds are free, if you did not ask about Rule 1.
Never had a complaint. Mostly because of Rule 2.

logs.title: Slate's shift
logs.text:
Slate fixed the reactor again today by sitting next to it.
I asked how. He said, 'I asked it.'
I asked what it said. He said, 'It was tired.'
Best engineer I ever had, and I don't understand a thing he does. Neither does the reactor. It runs better, though.

logs.title: Back in 5
logs.text:
Gone to look at the next rock. Back in 5 minutes.
Left the lamp on. Left the sacks. Left a note on the airlock in case.
If you're reading this and I'm not back, I found a good vein. Take it.
Don't take the sacks. The sacks are mine.

logs.title: Collection
logs.text:
We took up a collection for Ma Gantry's birthday. 4,100 credits, in small coins, for the good cake.
Ma counted it twice and said, 'That's exactly what you owe me. Thank you.'
Then she ate the cake.
It was a good cake. We didn't get any.

logs.title: Bay 4 rota
logs.text:
Cargo bay fights are now scheduled. Tuesdays: cousins. Thursdays: in-laws. Saturdays: anyone.
Bring your own chair. We have run out of chairs.
The winner gets the good wrench for a week.
The wrench is, in fact, not that good.

logs.title: Requisition 1,400
logs.text:
Requisition for pencils: 1,400. Reason: none left.
Response: DENIED. Reason: pencil shortage.
I have filed an appeal against the denial, in pencil.
It is the last pencil. I shall return it after the appeal.

logs.title: Patrol log, personal
logs.text:
I joined to inspect the Lattice. I inspect cargo.
The cargo is mostly honest. The captains are mostly not. The ratio is better than I expected.
Today a Scrapper gave me tea in a mug that said WORLD'S OKAYEST OFFICER.
I kept the mug. It is the only award I have ever had.

logs.title: Annex 9: Salvage Rights
logs.text:
Clans' position: finders keepers.
Concord's position: ownership persists.
Compromise reached after eleven hours: the wreck shall be called 'the wreck'.
Both sides left satisfied. Neither will say with what.

logs.title: Maintenance, deck 4
logs.text:
Floors polished: 4 decks, daily.
No one has asked us to stop. We have decided that is permission.
The alternative is to think about what the floors are being kept clean for.
The floors are very clean.

logs.title: The first note
logs.text:
The buoy sings because someone must.
The first note is a question. The second is also a question.
The third is an answer, and the answer is whoever is listening.
We will not say more. It would spoil the arrival.

logs.title: Garden, unattended
logs.text:
The plants lean toward a light no instrument sees.
We stopped weeding. It seemed rude.
The drone waters them on schedule. We have not told it the schedule has ended.
It has not told us either.

logs.title: For the apprentice
logs.text:
Do not ask what the crystal is for.
Ask what it is afraid of.
Then put it down, gently, and let it finish.
The ones who learn this become engineers. The rest become very good gardeners.

logs.title: Complaint, engine room
logs.text:
To the Prism, from the Emberkin staff: the engine room is cold.
The thermostat says 40 degrees. We say cold. Please send a little war.
The human crew say it is too hot. We have noted it.
We have noted also that humans are always cold, and then complain.

logs.title: A word on ion
logs.text:
The neon does not like the ion.
We are told it is the same physics that broke the gate, and the neon remembers.
Do not say this in front of the engines.
They have heard, and they have been very quiet since.

logs.title: Matched speed
logs.text:
Matched speed with the green-lit one. Looked in the galley window.
Table laid for eleven. Eleven chairs pushed back, like they'd all stood up at once.
Eleven bowls. Steam still coming off every one.
Nobody on the bridge. Nobody on the stairs. We didn't dock, we didn't wave, and we didn't have the decency to be scared until we were home.

logs.title: Roll call, satisfactory
logs.text:
Boarded the contact at 14:06. Air good. Lights on. Galley warm.
Manifest recovered from the console: eleven names.
Roll call held in the corridor, as procedure requires.
Response: eleven present. Observed: none.
Filed under 'Roll Call, Satisfactory'. I have no other form that fits.

logs.title: Tuff
logs.text:
Tuff went aboard the green-lit one for ten minutes.
Came back and sat in the airlock with his back to the wall. Wouldn't say why.
He says the engine room was the cleanest thing he has ever seen.
He says he has never been so scared. He's been fixing ours all week, as if to apologise to them.

logs.title: The unfinished
logs.text:
It hums the fourth note.
We have only taught the Prism three.
Whoever finished the song has no mouth that we can find.
We have begun to hum back. The Warden asks that we stop. We have asked the Warden what it hears.

logs.title: Recorder, verbatim
logs.text:
Transcribed from the contact's flight recorder, verbatim.
06:00. All well. Crew: all present.
06:00, next day. All well. Crew: all present.
14,609 entries, no variation. The 14,610th, dated today:
All well. Crew: all present. Visitors: noted. Welcome aboard.

logs.title: Count
logs.text:
The door stood open eleven seconds.
The table was laid for eleven.
We do not say these are the same eleven. We say we have counted.
We say also that we have stopped counting, and begun to listen.
